purpose: Parametric templates for the objects a provenance-led scene has to draw. NOT meshes: a mesh is someone's guess at a tree. Each template is a shape family, the measurable that sets its size, the relation between them, and the PROSAIL inputs it implies, with every parameter carrying its basis so a renderer can say which numbers were measured and which were assumed.
how_to_use: Fit every `fit_locally` relation on your own ground before drawing anything. You have heights (ICESat-2 h_canopy) and crown widths (sub-metre imagery) over the same objects, so the allometry is a measurement you can make rather than a citation you have to trust. An `assumed_range` is a placeholder that must be declared in the render's provenance, never presented as measured.

basis_vocabulary.measured: fitted on this landscape from a named instrument, with n and a residual
basis_vocabulary.fit_locally: the form is given, the coefficients are yours to fit; do not ship the default
basis_vocabulary.assumed_range: a plausible range from general knowledge; declare it, never claim it
basis_vocabulary.derived: computed from other parameters by a stated relation

cross_checks.shadow: shadow_length_m = height_m / tan(sun_elevation_deg), cast toward (sun_azimuth_deg + 180) mod 360; subtract the off-nadir lean height_m * tan(view_incidence_deg) along view_azimuth before comparing to a plan-view outline. Sun and view geometry per granule: x-emem-scene-sun and x-emem-scene-view on emem.dev scene routes.
cross_checks.reflectance: crown LAI and leaf-angle distribution feed PROSAIL; the forward run at the granule's own geometry must reproduce the measured reflectance after downsampling to the sensor's support.
cross_checks.storey: a built object's height and its floor count must agree at the declared storey height; disagreement is a finding, not a rounding error.

trees._note: Species of the western Ganga plain. Crown shape drives the shadow; deciduousness drives the calendar; LAI and leaf angle drive the reflectance. The same height parameter is testable by shadow AND by PROSAIL, which is why these are the templates to build first.
trees._allometry_form: crown_diameter_m = a * height_m^b, fitted per species on this landscape. Report a, b, n and the residual spread. Do not use a published coefficient from another region as if it were measured here.

crown_depth_ratio.note: crown depth as a share of total height

phenology.leafless_window: dry season, typically Jan-Mar in this belt
phenology.test: its NDVI floor must drop in that window; if it does not, the class is wrong or the pixel is mixed

phenology.note: brief leaf exchange; the NDVI floor stays high, which is exactly why it confuses a floor-and-swing tree rule with standing cane

mangifera_indica.note: an orchard is a REGULAR lattice; its row spacing is a measurable period in the image and a strong control on any orchard classification

allometry.note: b is markedly lower than for the broad-crowned species; a single pooled fit across species will be wrong for both

eucalyptus_spp.note: narrow crown and tall habit make this the best shadow-test subject in the landscape: the shadow is long and the crown is small, so the two measurements are nearly independent

planting_context: block plantation with an intercrop beneath
populus_deltoides.note: poplar agroforestry carries a crop UNDER the canopy; a pixel here is two layers and a single-layer inversion will be wrong in a stated direction

storey_height_m.note: the cross-check: height_m should equal num_floors * storey_height_m within one parapet

rcc_flat_roof_house.footprint_source: Overture buildings via emem /v1/building_footprints, each carrying its GERS id

height_availability.note: measured 2026-09-15: Overture release 2026-08-19.0 returns height on 262 of 276 buildings in a Manhattan test bbox and 0 of 691 in a Delhi bbox. Absence here is real, not an unread column. Derive height from floors where floors exist, else declare it assumed.

bull_trench_brick_kiln.geometry: oval trench footprint plus a single tall chimney
bull_trench_brick_kiln.note: the characteristic tall built object of this district and the most recognisable landmark a viewer will check. Its chimney casts the longest built shadow in the scene, so it is the best built-object shadow control; and its firing season is a thermal and aerosol signature.
bull_trench_brick_kiln.cross_check: chimney shadow length at a winter sun is tens of metres, which is several Sentinel-2 pixels; predicted and observed should agree before any tree shadow is trusted

tube_well_and_channel.geometry: small pump structure plus a linear channel to the field
tube_well_and_channel.note: not visually significant at 10 m, but it explains irrigation timing, which is a calendar feature; place from the channel, not from the structure

tree_row_on_bund.geometry: a line of crowns at a spacing, on a raised bund

spacing_m.note: measurable as a period along the row in sub-metre imagery

tree_row_on_bund.note: the row, not the individual tree, is the detectable object at 10 m: a row casts a continuous band tens of metres wide and hundreds long, in a direction the granule predicts

canal_with_bund.note: water surface is a specular reflector: at the specular angle it should brighten, which falsifies a water classification

cart_track.note: a 3 m track in a 10 m pixel is about a third of it, which is the unclaimed-fraction signature already used to call a pixel lane or bund

placement.rule: Never place an object where no measurement puts it. Every instance carries the fact or facts that located it, and an instance with no locating fact belongs to a separate, declarable scene-dressing layer.
placement.trees: from the tree-class pixels, refined to crowns by sub-metre texture where available; a crown whose predicted shadow is absent in the granule is a candidate for removal, not for a bigger crown
placement.buildings: from Overture footprints by GERS id, so an instance is traceable to a global entity a third party can look up
placement.rows: along measured field boundaries with a measured ploughing direction; the row's azimuth is a measurement, not a styling choice
placement.density: if your instance count exceeds what the classified pixel area supports, you are decorating. State instances-per-hectare against class-area-per-hectare and let the number be visible.
